description: Controlled subjects with declared defects, plus this repository's own artwork. Covers every failure mode T-012, T-018 and T-013 found, aimed rather than exhaustive: negative controls, the 1px-margin trap, the 4-vs-8 connectivity decision, the compactnessQ gate, the multi-frame rules, and §4.2 in two parts — the form-conformance term as a straight band against a form-following contour, a level set against both and a straight terminator on a straight-edged form, then one case per single-code defect in §4.2's issue table, so that a hue-carried form, a crushed shadow and a blown highlight are each something a case says they mean. Every expectation here is derived by hand from docs/EVALUATION.md and the declared geometry of the case, never copied out of the pipeline's own output.

cases.label: A 10x8 block with a 3px margin all round: one mass, nothing touching an edge

defects.note: Nothing injected. The baseline negative control: an analyzer that fires here is worse than one that misses a defect.

cases.label: A standing figure whose legs are joined to the body and split from each other: the gap is a background channel, not a hole

defects.note: Nothing injected. The second negative control, and the one that pins the holes/background pairing from the other side: a deliberate gap between two legs is exactly the shape a 4-connected background would call a hole.

cases.label: A 32x32 figure built from six overlapping rectangles: head, torso, two arms, two legs

defects.note: Nothing injected. Six rects rather than one, because a union of rectangles is where a naive component count goes wrong: five of the six touch the others only along an edge, and the pair of legs does not touch at all without the torso joining them.

cases.label: A 48x16 banner on a non-square 64x24 canvas: the UI slice, and a canvas that is not square

defects.note: Nothing injected. Present because docs/EVALUATION.md 6.3 asks for non-square canvases and because a threshold that only works at 32x32 is not a threshold.

cases.label: A solid body with a 0.39-alpha glow beside it: partial alpha is counted and never scored

defects.note: Nothing injected. Pins the ALPHA_SOLID decision from context.ts: a glow at 0 < alpha < 128 is a design decision, not a body part, so it must not enter N, must not change components, and must not become part of a contour. The glow is placed clear of the body on purpose: the first version of this case overlapped it, and the composited overlap stopped being partial alpha, which is a second and much less obvious way for a fixture to teach the wrong thing.

cases.label: A 16x16 disc on 32x32 with the outline command grown one pixel outside it

defects.note: Nothing injected. Exists for its connectivity count, and it refines docs/EVALUATION.md 3.3's prose: a CLOSED contour is 4-connected, because every turn is joined by the corner pixel. The claim that a 1px contour is '8-connected and 4-disconnected' holds for a staircase RUN, which is what connectivity/contour-staircase-24 isolates, and not for a closed ring.

cases.label: A 12px 1px diagonal run from (2,2) to (13,13): one component under 8-connectivity, twelve under 4

defects.note: 12 components under the subject rule, so the analyzer is right to say so: a shape whose parts touch only at a corner falls in half at 0.5x scale.
compactnessQ 65. A 1px diagonal is the thinnest thing a sprite can be.
Largest piece is 1 of 12 px.

cases.label: Two 5x5 blocks meeting at a single corner: one mass under 8-connectivity, two under 4

defects.note: One stray of 25 px against a 50 px subject, so the -75 row fires. share is exactly 500/1000, which is why fragmented-silhouette must NOT fire: the comparison is strict.

cases.label: A 5x5 block with one pixel punched out and a corner erased, so the pocket reaches the outside through a diagonal only

defects.note: Nothing injected, and that is the finding: the 1px pocket at (3,3) IS a hole under 4-connectivity and is NOT a hole here, because the erased corner at (2,2) is 4-connected to the outside and 8-connected to the pocket. The test proves the discriminating half by running the same flood with a 4-connected background and getting 1.

cases.label: An 18px 1px diagonal run on 24x24: the configuration docs/EVALUATION.md 3.3 describes for a contour

defects.note: 18 components under 4-connectivity.
compactnessQ 44.
Largest piece is 1 of 18 px.

cases.label: A 12x12 body with a 3x3 speck floating four pixels away from it

defects.note: One stray of 9 px against a 153 px subject: past the 2/100 stray ratio, so the -75 row.

cases.label: A body with a hat floating three rows above it: one dominant mass, so not fragmented

defects.note: One stray of 24 px against a 120 px subject. share is 800/1000, comfortably clear of the fragmented-silhouette floor, so this is the counter-case to defect/three-masses-20: two components, and only one of the two codes fires.

cases.label: Three blocks of 25, 20 and 15 px: no dominant mass, and the score floors at 0

defects.note: Two strays, so the -150 row rather than -75.
Largest is 25 of 60 px, share 417/1000. Blocking at severity 0.70.

cases.label: A 20x20 body with one pixel punched out: the area <= 3 clause of interior-hole

defects.note: A 1 px hole, which fires the 'any hole with area <= 3' clause rather than the ratio clause. Half of defect/interior-hole-window-24's contrast pair.

cases.label: The same body with a 6x6 window cut out: the holeRatio clause of interior-hole

defects.note: A 36 px hole, which is past the 'area <= 3' clause and so fires only because holeRatio is 99/1000. The other half of the contrast pair: same body, same code, same -100, from a different clause.

cases.label: A 12x12 ring with an 8x8 hole: the documented false positive, a deliberately hollow asset

defects.note: A 64 px hole in an 80 px ring. docs/EVALUATION.md 4.1 names this as a known false positive that a human rater's note settles, and no measurement can tell a keyhole from a mistake. In the corpus it is a defect like any other, because the mechanical rule is the mechanical rule.
compactnessQ 157: a 1px wall really is thin, whatever the wall is for.

cases.label: Ink running to three canvas edges with a 2px guard on the fourth: measured, and blocking

defects.note: borderTouch 3, severity 0.80, blocking. This is the exact boundary of SUBJECT_REQUIRED_MARGIN: 2px of guard is a margin somebody chose, so the dimension applies, and a shape cropped on three sides IS clipped. The two neighbours in the margin-guard pair show what happens at 0px and 1px.

cases.label: A 12x12 subject inside a 64x64 canvas: under a quarter of an edge on both axes

defects.note: span 188/1000. The comparison is an OR of two strict `<` tests, so a subject under a quarter on EITHER axis is undersized.

cases.label: A 16x16 canvas with nothing on it: every dimension reports 1000 and one blocking issue fails it

defects.note: docs/EVALUATION.md 5.3's demonstration. A blank canvas is not bad artwork, it is NO artwork, and a mean cannot express that: the score is 1.00 and the verdict is fail. This case exists so that a change which turns the blank canvas into a low score, or into an exclusion, fails.

cases.label: A 32x32 canvas inked edge to edge: no subject, so no silhouette is reported at all

defects.note: Nothing was injected; this is the ten real full-bleed scenes in miniature, and it is where T-012's bug lived. Measured on its own the mask scores 800 with a blocking shape-clipped, because borderTouch is 4 whenever ink runs to the frame. The report does not say that: it says the dimension does not apply, and records why. T-015 moved this expectation from fail to warn, and the move is a property of the aggregate rather than of the picture. silhouette is EXCLUDED here with no-subject, because a full-bleed subject has no outline to read; before noise was registered the measured set was {value 400} and the verdict was fail. noise applies to a full-bleed document and reads 1000, so the third dimension netted a clean reading against the first dimension abstention. warn still says what the case exists to say - not a perfect subject - and whether an abstention should be netted at all is an aggregator question this task does not own.

cases.label: The same ink with a single transparent row at the bottom: still no subject, and the raw measurement is still 800

defects.note: Nothing injected. The knife-edge T-018 found and solved: identical ink, one pixel of frame, and the predicate has to answer 'cannot measure' rather than 'a perfect subject'. The measure block below is the measurement that was never delivered, which is why the corpus records measurements even for excluded cases. T-015 moved this expectation from fail to warn, and the move is a property of the aggregate rather than of the picture. silhouette is EXCLUDED here with no-subject, because a full-bleed subject has no outline to read; before noise was registered the measured set was {value 400} and the verdict was fail. noise applies to a full-bleed document and reads 1000, so the third dimension netted a clean reading against the first dimension abstention. warn still says what the case exists to say - not a perfect subject - and whether an abstention should be netted at all is an aggregator question this task does not own.

cases.label: The same ink inset by 2px on all four sides: a subject, measured, and clean

defects.note: Nothing injected. The other end of the margin-guard pair: 2px is a margin somebody chose, so the dimension applies, and what it then has to say is 'clean', not 'perfect'. Without this case the pair would only show the exclusion and a reader could not tell whether the predicate also mis-handles a real subject.

cases.label: Two frames: a clean 8x8 block, then three separate masses. The dimension carries the worst frame

defects.note: Frame 1 only: two strays, so -150.
Frame 1 only: largest is 25 of 54 px. Blocking.

§4.6, and it is a real fact about this case rather than an accident of it: frame 0 is a 64px block and frame 1 is three masses totalling 54px, so `areaSpread` is `rhu(10 * 1000, rhu(118, 2)) = rhu(10000, 59) = 169` against §4.6's 150 gate. Blocking at 0.60.

cases.label: Three byte-identical frames: motion cannot be measured, and the hold is not a gate failure

defects.note: Severity 0.35, non-blocking, alongside excluded.motion = 'no-motion-content'. Not redundant: the exclusion says the dimension cannot be measured here, and the advisory says four copies of frame 0 is usually an agent that meant to animate and did not. Measured honestly, an identical sequence is a PERFECT animation, which is why the decision is the aggregator's and is made before the analyzer runs.

cases.label: Two frames, the second blank: the sheet exports as a hole and one blocking issue says so

defects.note: Severity 1.00, blocking. Note what does NOT happen: silhouette is still applicable (frame 0 has a subject, and exclusion is unanimity over inked frames, never a majority), and the blank frame is not scored rather than being scored 0, because 0 would mean 'measured, and it is bad'.

cases.label: A six-frame walk loop on a 40x32 canvas: even churn on every transition including the seam, and no motion code at all

defects.note: Nothing injected, and this is the case the whole `motion` corpus was missing: a declared-clean control on a SEQUENCE rather than on a single frame. §4.6's severity scale is the only one in the document that cannot be checked from a contact sheet, so a control that only ever drew stills left every motion reading uninterpretable — there was nothing to compare a firing case against. The loop is deliberately not trivial. Every transition, the seam included, moves exactly 96 of the canvas's 240 solid pixels (`churn [96 96 96 96 96 96]`, seam 96), the area is 240 on all six frames (`areaSpreadQ 0`), the centroid steps 4px in-loop and 4px at the seam (`seamStep 256` against `maxStep 256`, so §4.6's `> 1.5x` clause is false by a factor of 1.5), the tone is held constant so `lumDelta` is 0 on all six transitions, and every frame is held 100ms. A control that was clean because nothing moved would prove nothing; this one moves a fifth of its own pixels on every single transition and still says nothing.

cases.label: The same walk with the sixth frame drawn three pixels off the return: the loop closes with the body further away than any in-loop step

defects.note: Severity 0.55, blocking. §4.6's `seamStep > maxStep * 1.5` with `seamStep >= 1.0px`, and the numbers are the hand-derivable ones: the in-loop steps are 4px (`maxStep 256` in 1/64px) and the return is drawn from 7px rather than 4px (`seamStep 448`), so `448 * 2 = 896 > 256 * 3 = 768`. **This case is also the measurement that `loop-seam-pop` does NOT fire here**, which is the point of drawing it on this shape rather than on an obvious one: the seam changes 168 pixels against a median of 96, and `168 * 20 = 3360` is exactly `35 * 96 = 3360`, so §4.6's pop trigger is inclusive and does not fire. The two gates are not the same gate, and a case that fired both would have proved nothing about either.

cases.label: The same walk with one frame drawn a step off in both axes: one internal transition moves three times the median

defects.note: Severity 0.50, blocking. §4.6's `churnMax > 2 * churnMedian` over the INTERNAL transitions only: `churn [96 96 224 224 96 96]`, median 96, so `224 > 192`. **The durations are deliberately uneven and that is stated rather than hidden.** §4.6's `timing-mismatch` row needs `allDurationsEqual` AND `deltaSpreadQ >= 600`, and a frame that jumps also makes `lumDelta` uneven, so an evenly-timed version of this exact drawing reports `frame-jitter` *and* `timing-mismatch` — two true statements, and one fixture cannot isolate either. Holding the frames 80/100/120/140/160/120ms (median 120, nothing past `3 * 120`, 720ms total) removes the second row without removing the first, so this case says what it declares.

cases.label: Four frames on the same pixels, the lit half brightening in even steps and then snapping back: a seam that pops in tone

defects.note: Severity 0.55, blocking. §4.6's own sentence names this shape: "a seam that pops in *colour* while the silhouette happens to match still gets caught", and it is the only way to land the primary ratio on a chosen integer without drawing a second shape. The silhouette is byte-identical across all four frames (`churn [0 0 0 0]`, so the mask reading is silent and `churnMedian` 0), while `lumDelta` is 25, 25, 25 and a seam of 75 — the lit half climbs three equal steps and is then drawn three steps' worth darker in a single frame. `75 * 20 = 1500` against `35 * 25 = 875` fires the code and `50 * 25 = 1250` makes it blocking, with the band at 500. **This case is also why `loop-seam-pop` and `loop-seam-jump` are separate cases:** a pop carried by position fires the jump row as well, because a rigid translation moves the centroid and the pixels by the same fraction, so a corpus that only had positional pops could never show the tone channel working.

cases.label: Every frame held 100ms over a glow that jumps bright, drops back, and moves a third of as far: uniform timing over uneven motion

defects.note: Severity 0.45, not blocking. §4.6's `allDurationsEqual and deltaSpread >= 600`, and both halves are load-bearing: the internal `lumDelta`s are 60, 60 and 15, so `deltaSpread = rhu((60 - 15) * 1000, 60) = 750`. **The seam is deliberately quiet** — the last frame is 15 `Lq` from the first against a median of 60, so `loop-seam-pop` does not fire and this case is about the clock rather than about the loop point. `timing-mismatch` is not reachable any other way: `deltaSpread` is measured over internal transitions only, and a document whose transitions all move the same amount of ink cannot have one whatever its durations say.

cases.label: The clean walk with one frame held four times as long as the rest

defects.note: Severity 0.35, **not** blocking. §4.6's `any duration > 3 * the median duration`, and the near-miss is the same drawing at 300ms: `300 > 300` is false, so a frame held exactly three times the median is deliberate timing rather than a stutter. Every other reading on this case is the clean control's, unchanged — same pixels, same churn, same seam — which is what makes it a timing case and not a movement one. This is also the case that needed the `durations` recipe op: `createSprite`'s default is a uniform 100ms on every frame, so a corpus that could only draw pixels could produce an animation that is perfectly timed and never one that is not.

cases.label: The clean walk held at 12ms a frame: a 72ms cycle, under §4.6's 80ms floor

defects.note: Severity 0.30, **not** blocking. §4.6's `loopMs < 80 or loopMs > 1200`, read on `6 * 12 = 72`. The near-miss is the same drawing at 14ms a frame: 84ms is inside the window, so the window has two sides and the other one is 1200ms, not 0. Nothing else about this case differs from `motion/clean-walk-40x32` — the pixels are the same and the churn is the same — so the report on the two differs by exactly this one code, which is the only evidence that the row reads timing and not movement.

defects.note: Sweep member. The roundest the sweep gets; the 30x2 member is the same rectangle twenty-six pixels shorter and nothing else changed.

defects.note: Sweep member. The most compact a rectangle can be: 4*pi*N/P^2 for a square is pi/4, so 785 is the ceiling of this whole family.

defects.note: Sweep member.

defects.note: Sweep member. 3:1, which is about as slender as a character silhouette gets before it stops reading.

defects.note: Sweep member.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x6 rect, compactnessQ 436

defects.note: Sweep member.

defects.note: Sweep member. The last member comfortably above the gate.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x4 rect, compactnessQ 326: the last member above the gate

defects.note: Sweep member, and the important one: 326 is 26 per-mille above the gate. A gate moved from 300 to 250 would have left this case passing; a gate moved to 330 would have failed it. The sweep exists so that a move can be argued about with the whole curve in front of the reader rather than with one asset.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 28x3 rect, compactnessQ 275: 25 below the gate, and 6 above the one real character sprite

defects.note: compactnessQ 275 is below the gate of 300, so thin-profile fires. This is the sweep's upper neighbour of artwork/verify/lantern-keeper.pixel at 269, and the pair of them is the closest thing this corpus has to saying 'the gate sits between these two'.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x3 rect, compactnessQ 260: 9 below the one real character sprite

defects.note: compactnessQ 260, the sweep's lower neighbour of the lantern keeper at 269. Together with sweep/rect-28x3 at 275 this brackets the real measurement with a 15-wide interval.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 34x3 rect, compactnessQ 234

defects.note: compactnessQ 234. A 1px blade at game scale; a shape this thin genuinely does not read, which is the case the gate is for.

cases.label: Calibration sweep: a 30x2 rect, compactnessQ 184: the slenderest member, and thickness-sweep's other half

defects.note: compactnessQ 184. The matched pair with sweep/rect-30x28 at 784: same width, same canvas, same 2px margin, and the ONLY difference is the height. compactnessQ separates them by 600 per-mille and scoreQ by 100, and the second number is the one to review: the whole -100 of thin-profile is doing that work, so the dimension distinguishes a blade from a slab by exactly one penalty step.

cases.label: The same 28x3 band, centred on a 32x32 canvas: a knife

defects.note: A 3px band, which is 94/1000 of the canvas's short side. Also subject-undersized, because 3*4 < 32: the two codes overlap exactly on a band, which is the honest reason both are printed on every row.
28 wide on a 32 canvas, so the subject spans under a quarter of the width — §3.7's `span < 0.25` in per-mille (94).

cases.label: The same 28x3 band, centred on a 1024x1024 canvas: a horizon

defects.note: The identical 84 pixels on a 1024x1024 canvas, so `compactnessQ` is 275 on both members — the shape descriptor is right not to move, it is the same drawing — while `thicknessQ` reads 3 against 94.
3*4 < 1024 by a wide margin, and the subject spans 498/1000 of the canvas at its widest, which is under §3.7's quarter.

cases.label: The 28x3 band magnified 32x, centred on a 1024x1024 canvas

defects.note: NEGATIVE contrast pair with `sweep/band-28x3-on-32`, and the pair is designed to come out at **zero**. This is the knife magnified 32x, and every ratio of two lengths in one sprite is invariant under uniform magnification, so every measurement is identical and every one of them should be: compactnessQ 275, thicknessQ 94, profileQ 94, scoreQ 700. The one column where they are 32x apart is `thicknessPx`, a pixel count rather than a ratio — 96 against 3. Separating them further would need a target resolution, which a `.pixel` document does not carry and this pipeline must not invent, so the limit is pinned as an expectation rather than left in a comment. A corpus that only carried the pairs it passes would be hiding this one.

96*4 < 1024, and the subject spans 875/1000 of the canvas at its widest, which is over §3.7's quarter — so this member is NOT subject-undersized on the span clause. It is declared anyway because 96*4 = 384 is not >= 1024... which is the same arithmetic; the code comes from the same gate on the short side, and both are printed on the row so a reader can see which clause fired.

cases.prompt: Rate the six dimensions on docs/EVALUATION.md's 1-5 scale and give one overall judgement of usable / needs-work / unusable. This is an item icon, not a character, and §4's anchors are written for shapes, so say what you had to reinterpret.

cases.label: A 32x32 hard-surface tile: a bevelled block, the value dimension's curvature-gate counter-case
cases.prompt: Rate the six dimensions and give one overall judgement. A tile is the case docs/EVALUATION.md 4.2 says it cannot judge well: its straight edges are not a sphere, so a curvature gate has to exempt it. If your silhouette score disagrees with your value score, say so in a note — that disagreement is the finding.

cases.label: A 64x64 full-bleed field with a horizon: a scene the analyzer declares UNMEASURABLE, rated by a human anyway
cases.prompt: Rate the six dimensions and give one overall judgement. Note that `evaluate` reports silhouette as excluded ('no-subject') for this image and delivers no silhouette number at all, because the ink reaches the frame. Score silhouette anyway, from the picture. If a human score exists for something the pipeline says it cannot measure, T-022 needs to know which side is wrong.

cases.label: Five straight 45-degree tone bands cut corner to corner across the same 25-row round body `pixel demo` draws, on 32x32

defects.note: The same five tones, the same contrast and the same body as `value/nested-contour-32`, banded on `x + y` instead of laid on as translations of the row table. Every boundary is a straight line across a round form, so the shape reads and the tone count is right, and the only thing wrong with it is that the boundaries do not follow the form. This is the half of §4.2's acceptance pair that should fail.

cases.label: The same body shaded with four nested translated contours — `pixel demo`'s own construction

defects.note: The correction to `value/straight-diagonal-32`, and the negative control for the form term. Nothing is injected: the same five tones on the same body, laid on as translations of the row table rather than as straight cuts — which is what `packages/cli/src/demo.ts` does, so the pair is drawn on the form the product actually ships. `absent` names `plane-crosses-form` because that is the one code the pair turns on.

cases.label: The same body shaded with true insets — four level sets of `dist`, 2px apart, the construction that looks like a target

defects.note: The level-set bias, as a control rather than as a claim. §4.2 measures the spread of `dist` along a plane boundary, and a level set has a spread near zero, so the specified term rated this the best possible construction and rated `value/nested-contour-32` the worst — even though the two are the same body with the same five tones, the same five planes and the same four boundaries. The report prints both: `spanQ unscored` reads 91 here against 909 there, and `crossesQ` is 0 on all four of these boundaries because a level set turns everywhere, which is the property the scored term was redesigned around. The 909 was 545 until `dirQ` was made invariant to whether a boundary closes, at which point all four boundaries here and all four in `value/nested-contour-32` read `crossesQ` 0, and the worst plane stopped being a worst plane at all. Two things about the drawing, both load-bearing. The insets are 2px apart, not 1px: a 1px level set is a line, no pixel of it has three same-tone orthogonal neighbours, and it is therefore not a plane at all — a 1px version of this case registered 34 tone regions and ZERO plane boundaries, because a 1px staircase contour is 8-connected and 4-disconnected, so its 33 fragments each read as a region of their own. And the four insets are drawn largest-first, because a deeper inset painted before a shallower one is overpainted by it: the other order leaves two tones on the canvas instead of five.

cases.label: A straight-edged box with a straight horizontal terminator: correct shading, and the curvature gate must spare it

defects.note: §4.2 says "a straight plane across a straight-edged form is correct, not wrong", and the curvature gate is the clause that delivers it. This is the gate's negative control and it is the only case that can catch a gate which has been made so permissive that it never fires anywhere.

cases.label: One lightness bucket in four hues: the form is carried by hue, which a game tint takes away

defects.note: Every interior boundary changes hue without changing `LqBucket`, so hue is doing the work tone should.
One bucket holds 1000/1000 of the solid pixels.
The four hues sit at Lq 117..119, so the range is 2 against a floor of 45.

cases.label: The lower 16 rows of the same body at Lq 9: the shadow side has run out of steps

defects.note: 16 of the body's 25 rows are at or below Lq 12, which is past the 30/100 share.

cases.label: The same form-following construction with its lightest plane run to white: the lit side has run out of headroom

defects.note: One plane of the same five, repainted at Lq 255 instead of 220. 159 of the body's 398 solid pixels are at or above Lq 243, which is 399/1000 against §4.2's 10/100 share. The only difference from `value/nested-contour-32` is that one swatch, which is what makes the two a §6.2 pair: the tone terms separate them and every shape reading is identical.

cases.label: A full-bleed 64x64 scene whose lit dome is shaded with a terminator that follows the dome's own curve: the construction §4.2 wants, on artwork with no subject to read

defects.note: The negative half of T-100's pair, and the only negative control that can catch a curvature reference which is so permissive that it judges every plane on every full-bleed scene. Its lit dome is drawn as a smaller ellipse over a larger one in the shadow swatch, so the lit/shadow boundary is a crescent concentric with the dome -- an offset of the form, which is the construction §4.2 admits and the one `value/level-set-32` already pins on a subject with a readable outline. Everything else is identical to `value/straight-band-over-terrain-64`, which is what makes the pair §6.2's cheapest kind of regression test: one property, two answers.

cases.label: The same full-bleed dome with a straight horizontal shadow band laid across its middle: a terminator that ignores the form it cuts

defects.note: The positive half of T-100's pair and of T-101's reason for existing, and the case the corpus could not hold until T-101 landed. Identical canvas, identical dome, identical five swatches to `value/terrain-following-terminator-64`; the one changed property is a 10px band at y=40 laid across the lit face instead of four crescents concentric with the dome. By hand from §4.2: the band is 10 rows of solid ink, so it is an area and not a dither artefact; the line at y=40 walks one direction only, so `dirQ` is 0 and `surplusQ` is 0 and `bendQ` is 0, which is the reading of a boundary that does not turn; and `crossesQ` is then exactly `splitQ`, because `bendQ` is the only thing that could have damped it. THE BAND IS AT THE DOME'S MIDDLE ON PURPOSE, and that is measured rather than decorative. `splitQ` is §4.2's only multiplier, so a straight cut that does not halve the form is damped toward 0 on purpose — that is the clause which makes a crescent safe. At y=34 two thirds of the dome is below the band, `splitQ` reads 501, and §4.2's table puts that in the `<= 600` band at `formQ` 550 with NO issue: a milder cut, scored as a milder cut. At y=40 the dome is roughly 700px above the band and 810 below against the band's 640, `splitQ` reads 676, past the 600 floor, and the code fires. Both rows are the same defect drawn with the same intent; the one that reports it is the one that actually bisects the form. Before T-100 §4.2 could not report this at all: the curvature gate read its curvature off the subject's own outline, which on a full-bleed document IS the canvas frame, so `curvedQ` was 0 against a gate of 250, every plane was exempt, and the dimension returned `unmeasured: { form: 'no-subject' }` over a straight cut through a curved form. Before T-101 it could report it at one row and not at another — 260 at y=34, 248 at y=40 — because the band's own straight cut sat in the denominator of the arc it crossed, so whether a defect was caught depended on where it had been drawn. That is not a gate, it is a coin toss.

cases.label: A 12x12 body with two single pixels of a far-off colour buried inside it: colourOrphans positive

defects.note: Two pixels of #8a6a2f inside a #3a2f2a body, each at least 4px from any edge of it, so nothing within Chebyshev 2 is the same lightness and neither pixel bucket is inside the range its surroundings span. N is 144 and the count is 2, so the ratio is 14/1000 against the "> 8/1000" trigger of 4.4. **The trigger is why there are two of them and not one**: at 16x16 a single stray reads 7/1000 and is correctly silent. Only stray-colour is declared here, because every other expectation in this file is derived by hand and the codes this body also produces are not the ones under test.

cases.label: Two ramp entries 8 apart on every channel, each covering 72 pixels: the flat near-duplicate penalty

defects.note: #3a2f2a and #3a3732 are exactly 8 apart on every channel, which is the "<= 8" clause of 4.4 read as reached rather than passed, and each covers 72 solid pixels against the ">= 8" floor. **The count cannot size this**: 4.4 makes it a flat -100 rather than a band, because two ramp entries three steps apart are a decision error rather than a frequency one, and this case is one pair. The two entries are drawn as flat fields rather than as a ramp because a ramp would put a boundary between them and colourOrphans would then have a gradient to disagree about.

cases.label: A 12x12 body with two single pixels floating two pixels clear of it: nothing solid within Chebyshev 1 of either

defects.note: The body ends at x=14 and both loose pixels are at x=16, so the nearest body pixel to either is Chebyshev 2 away and nothing solid lies within Chebyshev 1: n8 == 0, which is §4.4's `isolated` — and the predicate `neighbourCounts` cannot satisfy at all unless a pixel is excluded from its own neighbour count. N is 144 + 2 = 146, so the ratio is rhu(2000, 146) = floor(2073 / 146) = 14 against the "> 8/1000" trigger, and 14 <= 20 puts isolatedQ on the 750 row. **Two and not one, and the trigger is why:** a single floating pixel is rhu(1000, 146) = 7, inside the trigger and correctly silent — the same arithmetic that puts two strays in `defect/stray-colour-16`. **The canvas is 18x18 on purpose:** two clear columns plus the body's 12 is 14, and on a 16-wide canvas the only column two away from a body ending at x=12 is x=14 — which is the last column, so the pixel would touch the border and `borderTouch` would fire. x=16 on 18 leaves the loose pixel interior with `borderTouch` 0, and the measurement under test is the neighbour count rather than a crop. **Dmax is 5** on a 12x12 body, so §4.4's thin-sprite doubling of the bounds does not apply and the 8/1000 trigger stands unchanged. **A floating pixel is also a detached component, and `detached-pieces` still does not fire:** §4.1's row needs `strayRatio > 2/100`, and two stray pixels of 146 is rhu(2000, 146) = 14/1000 — 1.4 per cent, inside the row — so the code is listed under `absent` and not declared here. That is a fact about §4.1's threshold rather than about this drawing, and it is recorded rather than tuned: §3.3 makes a threshold a product decision, and no cut on this count separates "two pixels somebody left behind" from "a deliberate second mass" without a question about intent that a pixel cannot answer. The two `value` codes are the fixture's, not the defect's: one bucket gives `flat-value` on `buckets <= 1` and `narrow-value-range` on `range 0 < 45`, while `colourOrphans` is 0 by §4.4's own exclusion — every body pixel has a same-bucket neighbour within Chebyshev 2, and the two loose pixels have no neighbours at all, which that predicate explicitly refuses to count because `isolated` is the measure for it.

cases.label: A 10x10 body with a two-pixel antenna hung off its right edge: the tip has exactly one solid 8-neighbour

defects.note: The antenna at (13,8) and (14,8) is 4-connected to the body, so the drawing is one component and `silhouette` has nothing to say about it. The tip at (14,8) has exactly one solid 8-neighbour — (13,8), orthogonally — which is §4.4's `spurs` and nothing else; the pixel behind it has two. N is 100 + 2 = 102, so the ratio is rhu(1000, 102) = floor(1051 / 102) = 10 against the "> 8/1000" trigger, and 10 <= 20 puts spurQ on the 750 row. **The canvas is 16x16 on purpose and this is the case's arithmetic, not its framing:** §4.4's trigger is a ratio of the solid count, so the identical drawing is rhu(1000, 146) = 7 on an 18x18 canvas — inside the trigger, with spurQ 900 and no code at all. A case drawn at that size would have been a green row proving nothing, and §3.2's "acceptance uses the discriminating case" is the whole argument for the 16x16. **Dmax is 4** on a 10x10 body, so the bounds are not doubled and the antenna does not make the subject a line sprite (`Dmax <= 1`); a line sprite would drop `spurs` from the measurement altogether rather than grade it. `isolated` and `diagOnly` are 0: the antenna's pixels each have one orthogonal neighbour, and every body pixel has at least two. **`perimeter` is 44 and not 46, and that is worth reading twice:** a 10x10 body alone has 40, the antenna pixel behind the tip adds 2 (up and down) and the tip adds 3 (up, down and the open side), but hanging the antenna on the body's right edge also *removes* one of the body's own 10 boundary transitions — the pixel at (12,8) no longer has a transparent neighbour to its right — so 40 - 1 + 2 + 3 = 44. `compactnessQ` is read off the subject's own numbers, `rhu(4*355*1000*102, 113*44*44) = 662`. The two `value` codes are the fixture's — one bucket, so `flat-value` on `buckets <= 1` and `narrow-value-range` on `range 0 < 45`.

cases.label: A 12x12 body with a six-pixel 1px diagonal run two columns clear of it: every pixel of the run touches the drawing diagonally only

defects.note: The run runs (16,2) to (21,7). The body ends at x=13, so the nearest body pixel to (16,2) is Chebyshev 3 away and nothing solid is within Chebyshev 1 of the run's first pixel; along the run every pixel reaches only its two immediate neighbours, and both are diagonal, so n4 == 0 on all six and n8 == 2 on the four interior pixels. That is §4.4's `diagOnly`, and its ratio is rhu(6000, 150) = floor(6075 / 150) = 40 against the "> 8/1000" trigger, landing in the `<= 50/1000` row at diagQ 500. **The body is load-bearing and not decoration.** A bare 1px run is a line sprite — `Dmax <= 1`, so §4.4 drops `isolated`, `diagOnly` and `spurs` from the measurement and `diagQ` is `null` — which is exactly why `connectivity/diagonal-bridge-16` and `connectivity/contour-staircase-24` cannot carry this code: their `diag` of 1000/1000 was a raw ratio nobody was ever shown. The 12x12 body beside the run holds Dmax at 5, so the sub-score exists and the issue can be raised.

**The run's two ends read `n8 == 1` as well** — (16,2) reaches only (17,3) and (21,7) only (20,6) — so `spurs` is 2 and the ratio is rhu(2000, 150) = 13, past the same trigger and into the same `<= 20/1000` row at spurQ 750. A 1px diagonal seam is simultaneously the shape `single-pixel-spur` names, and that is a true property of the drawing rather than a defect in it: the run has two endpoints and an endpoint of a 1px chain has exactly one neighbour by construction. It is declared here because `expect.codes` is an exact match, and left declared rather than suppressed because hiding it would be a fixture that disagrees with its own note.

The run is 8-connected and 4-disconnected, so §4.1's `components` — 4-connected, per §3.3 — reads **7**, not 2: the body and six singletons. That is the same reading `connectivity/diagonal-bridge-16` already carries, and the row is worth checking against it rather than against the eye. 6 stray pixels of 150 is `rhu(6000, 150) = 40/1000`, past §4.1's `> 2/100` strayRatio, and `strayCount` 6 is `>= 2`, so the -150 row is the one that applies. §4.4's message for the two codes above is the same fact from two angles — at half scale, under a filter, or on a CRT a diagonal contact disappears — and both are the truth about this drawing. **The -450 adjustment floor is not reached:** the total is -150, `share` is rhu(144000, 150) = 960/1000 which is `>= 90/100` and `< 98/100`, so the base is the 900 row and `scoreQ` is 750. **`fragmented-silhouette` does not fire** — its own row needs `share < 0.50` and the largest piece is 144 of 150 — so the six strays cost 150 per-mille and no code that blocks delivery.

cases.label: Six declared hue families 60 degrees apart on a 32x32: one below §4.3's `hue-sprawl` gate of seven, and drawn entirely from the palette

defects.note: **The negative control for `hue-sprawl`, and the first half of the `palette/hue-sectors` contrast pair.** Six vertical bands at hues 0, 60, 120, 180, 240 and 300, every one of them a declared swatch. §4.3's row is `hueSectors >= 7` on a canvas that is not `scene`-class, so this reads 6 and says nothing; the partner `defect/hue-sprawl-32` is the identical construction with a seventh band at hue 30 and differs by exactly that one band. **The colours are spread in luminance as well as hue by construction** (`Lq` 40 to 137 across the six), so `value` sees six tone regions and a range of 164 rather than a flat field — with six colours of one luminance it would fire `flat-value`, and a negative control that carries a code has stopped being one.

cases.label: The same six bands plus a seventh at hue 30: seven 30-degree sectors on a `compact` canvas, and nothing else wrong

defects.note: A seventh 3px band at `#c08000`, hue 30, which is sector 1 — and sector 1 is not among the six the partner case uses (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10), so `hueSectors` is **7** and §4.3's `>= 7` row fires. Everything else about the drawing is clean and is asserted rather than assumed: `offPalette` 0, `distinctColours` 7 against the `compact` budget of 16, `muddy` 0 because nothing is off the palette, `maxNearestDistance` 0 because every band is a swatch, and a mean saturation of 100% so `grey-colours` is silent. **The class is the only exemption §4.3 gives this row**, so the same seven families on a 256x256 canvas are not reported; `docs/EVALUATION.md` §7 records that as item 8's standing complaint, and the corpus measures the other side of it rather than arguing it.

cases.label: Three bands at a mean saturation of 10% of full carrying one hue family: §4.3's `grey-colours` conjunct, on its own

defects.note: **The negative control for `grey-colours`, and the one that isolates the conjunct.** §4.3's row is `meanSat < 15/100` **and** `hueSectors >= 3`. This drawing satisfies the first clause absolutely: `#e8d9a0` at `s255 79` over two pure greys at `s255 0` gives a mean of 26.3 of 255, which is **10.3% of full**, well under the gate. What it does not have is three hue families — `hueSectors` is 1, because §3.4 counts a hue family only at `s255 >= 12` and the two greys are at 0. So a washed-out palette with one hue is disciplined, and a gate written as "low saturation" without the conjunct would fire on it. The partner `defect/grey-washed-hues-32` is the same construction with three tints of three hues and **is** reported.

cases.label: Four bands: a skin tone and three tints at `s255 15` in three different 30-degree sectors, so the hues are present and washed out

defects.note: `#807878`, `#788078` and `#787880` each have `s255 = floor(8 * 255 / 128) = 15`, which is `>= 12` and so counts as a hue family, at hues 0, 120 and 240 — sectors 0, 4 and 8. With the skin band the sprite has **four** hue families and a mean `s255` of 15, i.e. **5.9% of full** against §4.3's 15% gate, and the row fires at -100. **This case is also the one that decides which document was right.** §4.3 defines `meanSat` as the mean `s255` divided by 255, so the integer test is `sumS255 * 100 < 15 * 255 * N`; §3.7 transcribed it as `sumS255 * 100 < 15 * N`, which asks for a mean `s255` below 0.15 and, `s255` being an integer, is satisfiable only by pixels that are *exactly* grey. On this drawing the first test is `900 * 100 < 15 * 255 * 576` (true) and the second is `900 * 100 < 15 * 576` (false), so with the old transcription in `palette.ts` this code could not have fired at all.

**A co-fire from `noise`, and it is not incidental.** The three tints differ by 8 per channel from each other, which is inside §4.4's Chebyshev 8 and over its `>= 8` pixel floor, so `nearDuplicatePairs` is 3. A washed-out palette is *made of* near-identical colours — that is what washed out means — so this code and `grey-colours` are two readings of one artwork from two different questions: one says "you have three hue families", the other says "two of them are the same colour". It is declared rather than hidden because `expect.codes` is an exact match and a fixture that disagrees with its own note is worse than one that is untidy.

cases.label: Sixteen declared greys on a 32x32, tiled 4x4: exactly §4.3's `compact` budget of sixteen, and nothing else wrong

defects.note: **The negative control for `colour-budget-exceeded`, and the near-miss half of its pair.** Sixteen greys 15 apart, so every pair is more than §4.4's Chebyshev 8 and `nearDuplicatePairs` is 0; they are **pure** greys (`s255 0`), so `hueSectors` is 0 and both `hue-sprawl` and `grey-colours` are silent on their own clauses; and all sixteen are declared, so `offPalette` and `muddy` are 0. `distinctColours` is exactly 16 and the budget is exactly 16, so §4.3's `>` does not fire — **a `>=` written for a `>` would pass this row and fail the next.** The partner adds one grey and differs by nothing else.

cases.label: The same tiling with a seventeenth grey: 17 distinct colours against a `compact` budget of 16

defects.note: One extra declared grey makes `distinctColours` 17 against §4.3's `compact` budget of 16, which is -200 and lands the dimension at 800. **The budget is keyed on canvas area and not on the solid count, and this pair is the evidence:** both members have `N` 576 on a 32x32 canvas and differ in nothing but how many swatches the artist declared. The tiling is 4x4 blocks rather than single pixels **on purpose** — thirteen one-pixel accents were measured first, and every one of them is a `colourOrphan` to §4.4, which fired `stray-colour` at 13 of 576 and made the case about `noise` instead of about `palette`. A 4x4 block has a same-bucket neighbour within Chebyshev 2 for every one of its pixels, so `colourOrphans` is 0 here.

cases.label: Four declared bands, one replaced by a colour a few channel steps off its swatch: a quarter of the ink is not in the palette

defects.note: The third band is `#9c9c36` where the declared swatch is `#a0a030` — four per channel. §4.3 defines off-palette as **exact** non-membership, not "not close to a swatch", so 144 of 576 pixels is `rhu(144000, 576) = 250` per-mille: the base is §4.3's `<= 40/100` row at 550, and the issue is **blocking** at severity 0.55 because 250 is above §4.3's 0.20. **This is the snapping-miss case the specification describes**, and it is deliberately *not* reported as `invented-colours`: the redmean distance from `#9c9c36` to the nearest swatch is 190 against §4.3's gate of 12000, and §4.3 exists to separate exactly those two failure modes. `defect/invented-colour-32` is the other half of that pair, and the reason it carries a *different* ratio for the same kind of mistake is §4.3's: how far off you are, not how much of you is.

cases.label: The same four declared bands with one pixel of `#ff0080` inside them: a colour 87019 away from every swatch

defects.note: A single pixel of magenta among 575 pixels of declared swatches. Its redmean distance to the nearest swatch is 87019 against §4.3's 12000, so `invented-colours` fires at severity 0.40 — **and `off-palette` does not**, because 1 of 576 is `rhu(1000, 576) = 2` per-mille, inside §4.3's `<= 2/100` row at 950. That isolation is the point: it is the only shape in the corpus where `invented-colours` is reachable on its own rather than as a passenger, and §4.3's justification for carrying the quantity at all is that it separates "one step off a ramp entry, one `quantize_to_palette` call" from "30000 away from every swatch, the fix is a decision". `noise` reads 1 `colourOrphan` here, which is `rhu(1000, 576) = 2` against §4.4's `<= 8/1000` row, so `stray-colour` does not fire.

cases.label: The same four bands with thirty pixels of undeclared olive in three 2x5 patches: off the palette and inside §3.4's muddy window

defects.note: `#605850` has `s255 = floor(16 * 255 / 96) = 42` and `v255 = 96`, so it is inside §3.4's window of `s255 <= 76` and `64 <= v255 <= 204`. Thirty such pixels of 576 is `rhu(30000, 576) = 52` per-mille against §4.3's `>= 5/100` = 50, and the row fires at -100. **The patches are 2x5 rather than one block so that `noise` sees nothing**: 30 pixels of a colour that nothing around it agrees with would be 30 `colourOrphans` and would carry `stray-colour` as well, and the case would then be about two dimensions at once.

**Declared because §4.3's own numbers make it unavoidable, and the arithmetic is the finding.** `muddy` is defined over *off-palette* pixels, so `muddyRatio <= offPaletteRatio` pixel for pixel and always; a muddy ratio of 50 per-mille is an off-palette ratio of at least 50, and §4.3's `off-palette` trigger is `> 2/100` = 20. **`muddy-mix` therefore cannot fire alone** — the nesting is in the threshold table rather than in the fixture, and a report that shows only one of the two has been shown a partial fact. At 52 per-mille the issue is the advisory 0.35 rather than the blocking 0.55.
